_comment: Budget gate for tools/run-slices.ps1. The driver reads this before EVERY slice, so editing
it takes effect immediately - no need to stop the driver.
TWO DIFFERENT JOBS, do not confuse them:
Slice caps are the rationing. They are what actually keeps the port to a defined share of
the allowance, and they are exact: the driver counts its own sessions.
Token caps are a circuit breaker, not a share. They exist to stop the driver on an
abnormally heavy day, and they are set well ABOVE typical usage on purpose.
The token figures are GLOBAL: every Claude Code session on this machine, and every token
type including cache reads, which dominate the total.
Calibrated 2026-08-29 from ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl. Typical usage on this machine is
about 2.9e9 tokens/day and 1.98e10/week by this metric. The caps below sit at roughly twice
the daily figure and 1.75x the weekly one. An earlier attempt to set them at HALF typical
usage was tested and rejected: the gate refused the very first slice, because an ordinary
working day passes that mark by the afternoon. A cap that never lets the driver start is not
a safeguard, it is a broken switch - so rationing lives in the slice caps and these numbers
Recalibrate after Phase 1: docs/plan/slice-log.jsonl records what each slice actually cost,
which is the tokens-per-slice figure the design spec asks to be measured and recorded. Set
maxSlicesPerDay from that number and the share of allowance you want the port to have.
